Export the tables of an analysis for a report or a paper

Source: R/export.R
da_export.Rd

da_export() writes the main tables of a result of this package (the analysis of variance, the components, the effects with their standard errors and tests, and so on) to a Word document, a LaTeX file of booktabs tables, an HTML page, a Markdown file or CSV files, with numbers rounded for print.

Usage

da_export(
  x,
  file,
  format = c("docx", "latex", "html", "markdown", "csv"),
  tables = NULL,
  digits = 3,
  title = NULL
)

da_tables(x, digits = 3)

Arguments

x

a result of Griffing, GriffingMeans, Hayman, PartialDiallel or another analysis of the package.

file

path of the file to write (its extension does not choose the format; format does).

format

"docx" (Word), "latex", "html", "markdown" or "csv".

tables

names of the tables to write (default all; see names(da_tables(x))).

digits

decimals of the printed numbers (default 3).

title

title written above the tables (default: the label of the analysis).

Value

da_export(): the path(s) of the file(s) written, invisibly. da_tables(): a named list of data frames.

Details

da_tables() returns the tables that da_export() writes, as a named list of data frames, so that they can be edited first. Numbers are rounded to digits decimals; p-values are printed with three decimals and as <0.001 below 0.001. Word documents need the packages officer and flextable; the other formats need nothing beyond base R. For LaTeX, the file holds one table environment per table and needs \usepackage{booktabs} in the preamble. For CSV, each table goes to its own file, named after file with the table name appended.

See also

Other DiallelAnalysisR utilities: da_notation(), da_reference(), da_save(), da_theme()

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

fit <-
  Griffing(
      y          = Yield
    , Rep        = Rep
    , Cross1     = Cross1
    , Cross2     = Cross2
    , data       = GriffingData1
    , Method     = 1
    , Model      = 1
    , Reciprocal = c("combined", "split")[1]
    )
names(da_tables(x = fit, digits = 3))
#> [1] "Analysis of variance"               "Components"                        
#> [3] "General combining ability effects"  "Specific combining ability effects"
#> [5] "Reciprocal effects"                 "Standard errors"                   
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tex")
da_export(
    x      = fit
  , file   = f
  , format = c("docx", "latex", "html", "markdown", "csv")[2]
  , tables = NULL
  , digits = 3
  , title  = NULL
  )
cat(readLines(f)[1:12], sep = "\n")
#> % Griffing's Method 1, Model 1 (fixed effects); 8 parents, 4 replicates
#> % tables written by DiallelAnalysisR::da_export(); needs \usepackage{booktabs}
#> 
#> \begin{table}[htbp]
#> \centering
#> \caption{Analysis of variance}
#> \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
#> \toprule
#> Source & Df & Sum Sq & Mean Sq & F value & Pr(>F) \\
#> \midrule
#> gca & 7 & 3804.643 & 543.520 & 18.887 & $<$0.001 \\
#> sca & 28 & 22060.789 & 787.885 & 27.378 & $<$0.001 \\
